source.source_summary: Fully original relationship drama about a woman discovering that her boyfriend secretly monetized anonymous videos based on their private arguments.

selected.title: My Boyfriend Was Monetizing Our Private Fights
selected.hook: My coworker quoted a fight I had only told my boyfriend about.
selected.voiceover:
My coworker quoted a fight I had only told my boyfriend about.

At lunch she laughed and said, ‘At least you didn’t hide the concert tickets in the freezer.’

I stopped eating.

Two nights earlier, my boyfriend and I had argued because he bought expensive tickets without telling me, so I hid them in the freezer out of frustration. Nobody else knew.

She showed me a relationship-advice account she follows.

Its latest video described our argument almost word for word.

No names. No faces. But there were dozens of posts.

Our missed anniversary. The fight about his ex texting him. The weekend I slept at my sister’s. Even why I’m scared of marriage.

The account had eighty thousand followers.

I confronted him that night.

He admitted the page was his.

He’d started posting ‘anonymous couple stories’ six months ago because people found them relatable. He was making money from our arguments.

I asked him to delete everything. He offered to stop posting new videos, but said deleting the old ones would destroy the account he had built.

That’s when I realized he was negotiating over my privacy like it was content inventory.

I packed a bag and left.

Now he says I’m ending our relationship over stories nobody could prove were about me.

Would the anonymity matter to you, or did he cross the line when he turned our private life into content?
selected.youtube_description:
A coworker repeats a bizarre detail from a private argument, leading a woman to a relationship-advice account with 80,000 followers. The creator never uses names or faces, but the stories are far too familiar — and the truth raises a messy question about privacy, money, and what partners are allowed to share online. Would anonymity make this acceptable to you?
